# Kourovka 6.17: varieties generated by groups with solvable word problem

For a surjective homomorphism $\varphi : F_n \to G$ from the free group on $n$ generators, the word problem of $G$ with respect to $\varphi$ is solvable when the set of words $w \in F_n$ with $\varphi(w) = 1$ is computable (decidable). Kourovka problem 6.17 (A. V. Kuznetsov) asks whether every variety of groups is generated by its finitely generated groups with solvable word problem. Representing a variety by its laws, a fully invariant subgroup $N$ of the free group $F_\infty$ on countably many generators, this says: for every such $N$ and every word $w \notin N$ there is a finitely generated group $G$, with a surjection $F_n \to G$ for which the word problem is solvable, such that $G$ satisfies every law in $N$ and $f(w) \neq 1$ for some homomorphism $f : F_\infty \to G$.
